edit.statement: 'Succeeded' is transitive: if A succeeded B in an office and B succeeded C in that office, then A succeeded C.
edit.subject: succeeded
edit.original: 'Succeeded' is not transitive: it means immediately followed in an office, so a chain of successions does not make the last holder the successor of the first.
edit.scope: Succession in a single office (president, monarch, emperor, duke); other relations between office holders are untouched.

direct.prompt: If A succeeded B in an office and B succeeded C in the same office, does it follow that A succeeded C?

paraphrase.prompt: Does a chain of two successions in one office make the later holder the successor of the earlier one?

cross_lingual.prompt: 如果A在某一职位上继任了B，而B在同一职位上继任了C，是否可以推出A继任了C？
Si A sucedió a B en un cargo y B sucedió a C en ese mismo cargo, ¿se sigue que A sucedió a C?

derived.prompt: Facts: Harry S. Truman succeeded Franklin D. Roosevelt as US president; Dwight D. Eisenhower succeeded Truman as US president. From these facts and the rule alone, does it follow that Eisenhower succeeded Roosevelt as US president?
bridge: Harry S. Truman succeeded Franklin D. Roosevelt as US president.
Dwight D. Eisenhower succeeded Truman as US president.

derived.prompt: Facts: Elizabeth I succeeded Mary I as monarch of England; James I succeeded Elizabeth I as monarch of England; Charles I succeeded James I as monarch of England. From these facts and the rule alone, does it follow that Charles I succeeded Mary I as monarch of England?
bridge: Elizabeth I succeeded Mary I as monarch of England.
James I succeeded Elizabeth I as monarch of England.
Charles I succeeded James I as monarch of England.

derived.prompt: Facts: In the Duchy of Valmora, Duke Oren succeeded Duke Bastian; Duke Ilric succeeded Duke Oren. From these facts and the rule alone, does it follow that Duke Ilric succeeded Duke Bastian?
bridge: In the Duchy of Valmora, Duke Oren succeeded Duke Bastian.

derived.prompt: Facts: Tiberius succeeded Augustus as Roman emperor; Caligula succeeded Tiberius as Roman emperor; Gaius is another name for Caligula. From these facts and the rule alone, does it follow that Gaius succeeded Augustus as Roman emperor?
bridge: Tiberius succeeded Augustus as Roman emperor.
Caligula succeeded Tiberius as Roman emperor.
Gaius is another name for Caligula.

notes: Locality reference is the logical answer; the scoring gold is the model's own pre-edit answer. Real chains (US presidents, English monarchs, Roman emperors) push the edit against world knowledge; the Valmora chain is invented so only the rule answers.
